decisions.reason: The page 15 photo-crop adjustment is owned by the photo-treatment Requirement and does not change the document's general layout or graphic-treatment attributes.
Making the tree more visible does not change the Agua Arc brand identity or required brand assets.
The photo-crop request does not affect any supplied table, table replacement, or table-integration behavior.
The page 15 image adjustment does not alter the requirement that hyperlinks function in the saved proposal.
The source concerns a photo on page 15, not the one-page cover letter, its signature, or relocation of its favored images.
Zooming out a page 15 photograph does not change narrative integration, fixed section order, or the unresolved inclusion of Section 6.
The image-crop revision does not change Canva access, editability, ownership, asset policy, or reuse rights.
The photo adjustment does not change the required PDF format, file count, email submission method, or export quality.
The source applies to the separate GreenLatinos RFQ proposal and does not affect the TPEC proposal-design requirement.
The client requests a different crop within an existing photograph but does not change the proposal's page-limit goal or reduction approach.
This is one revision instruction to be handled within the existing revision process; it does not change the number or trigger of revision rounds.
The page 15 photo-crop request does not alter any draft, revision, submission, or deadline timing.
